title: The Regiment of Port Mahon
premise: In the winter of 1712, as the War of the Spanish Succession grinds toward uncertain peace, the garrison town of Port Mahon is cut off when the season's storms close the only bridge to the mainland. Cyrus Almeida, a nurse who secretly records the names of the common soldiers that officers erase from official dispatches, finds her ledger becoming the town's true history. When an armistice delegation arrives and only one berth remains on the last ship out, Cyrus must choose between her ailing brother, the orphaned girl she has come to love, and the colonel whose corruption she has documented. In the end she gives up the berth herself, stays through the siege's final fever, and learns that belonging is not granted by escape but by who remains to remember.
about_author: Odile Nystrom is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military hospital records in Mediterranean port towns. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Cyrus Almeida tends wounded soldiers in Port Mahon's overcrowded infirmary, recording in a hidden ledger the names officers strike from dispatches. Her brother Tomas begs her to leave before winter. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet defiance — she believes history happens elsewhere, but keeps count anyway.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Autumn storms collapse the causeway approach; the governor declares the road shut until spring. Supply wagons halt, and the garrison's mood sours. POV: Sergeant Ivo Brandt, who delivers the news. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine — the island becomes a trap no one has named yet.

chapters.title: Colonel Vasseur's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Cyrus treats men wounded in a pointless skirmish ordered by Colonel Vasseur to burnish his record for the coming armistice talks. She adds eleven names to her ledger. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counts Cannonballs
chapters.summary: A shell-shocked orphan, Nell, takes refuge in the infirmary and counts everything to keep calm. Cyrus, childless and guarded, begins teaching her letters using the ledger itself. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: fragile warmth — two people building a family from scraps.

chapters.title: Rations and Rumors
chapters.summary: Bread goes short; rumors claim the armistice will abandon the garrison entirely. Tomas falls ill with the fever moving through the lower town. POV: Ivo, who must enforce rationing on starving neighbors. Emotional beat: shame of complicity — following orders begins to cost.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Vasseur discovers a discrepancy between casualty reports and burial counts and suspects a leak. He interrogates the infirmary staff; Cyrus lies smoothly for the first time. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve — the ledger is now worth dying over.

chapters.title: The Delegation Arrives by Sea
chapters.summary: An armistice delegation lands at the harbor, escorted by a single ship — the last vessel guaranteed passage before ice closes the roads entirely. One civilian berth is allotted to the town. Hope and resentment ignite together. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dangerous hope.

chapters.title: Tomas's Bargain
chapters.summary: Feverish but lucid, Tomas asks Cyrus to secure the berth for him, arguing he can carry her ledger to the mainland and publish it. She cannot tell if he wants to save her work or himself. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Nell's Name Is Not Written
chapters.summary: Cyrus realizes Nell appears nowhere in any register — not the parish rolls, not the garrison lists. Officially the girl does not exist, and so cannot be given the berth. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: heartbreak of invisibility — being uncounted has a price.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo discovers Vasseur keeps his own book: payments taken to falsify supply manifests while the town starves. The colonel offers Ivo a share and silence. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: temptation — corruption dressed up as prudence.

chapters.title: The Fever Wall
chapters.summary: Typhus sweeps the lower town; the infirmary becomes a ward of the dying. Cyrus works three days without sleep, writing names by candle stub. Tomas worsens. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured — the ledger becomes a vigil.

chapters.title: A Ship That Cannot Wait
chapters.summary: The delegation announces the ship departs in nine days, armistice signed or not. After that, nothing leaves until thaw. The town turns on itself; the berth becomes currency. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: ticking clock — scarcity makes monsters of neighbors.

chapters.title: Blackmail in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Vasseur corners Cyrus, having deduced the ledger's existence, and offers a trade: the berth for the book. He needs her silence more than he admits. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vertigo — the thing she protected could buy her brother's life.

chapters.title: Ivo Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Ivo copies pages of Vasseur's corruption ledger and passes them to Cyrus, choosing conscience over career. They become reluctant allies. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: redemption's first step — costly, irreversible.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Cyrus faces the choice plainly: Tomas, dying and deserving; Nell, invisible and blameless; or herself, the keeper of the record. Each argument indicts the others. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: moral crucible — every option is a betrayal.

chapters.title: The Riot at the Gate
chapters.summary: Starving townsfolk storm the harbor stores; soldiers fire. Among the dead is the priest who baptized half the town. Vasseur blames saboteurs and tightens martial law. POV: Nell, hiding in the belfry. Emotional beat: horror witnessed small — history through a child's eyes.

chapters.title: Tomas's Confession
chapters.summary: Near death, Tomas admits he already sold information about the ledger to Vasseur's aide weeks ago — the trade offer was theater. He asks forgiveness. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief without anger — betrayal born of desperation, not malice.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Armistice
chapters.summary: Delegates initial the armistice terms; the garrison will be withdrawn but civilians abandoned until spring. Cyrus decides: she puts Nell's name on the berth, forged papers and all, and sends the ledger with her. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — she chooses the future over the past.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: At dawn the ship sails. Nell screams Cyrus's name from the rail; Tomas dies quietly as the sails shrink. Vasseur discovers the ledger gone and orders Cyrus arrested. POV: alternating Cyrus and Nell. Emotional beat: severance — love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Colonel
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Cyrus confronts Vasseur, revealing she mailed duplicate ledger pages to the delegation's chief commissioner weeks earlier. His corruption surfaces even as the ink on the armistice dries. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph — truth arrives too late to save, never too late to name.

chapters.title: What the Thaw Brings
chapters.summary: Spring opens the road. Vasseur is recalled in disgrace; Ivo testifies and loses his commission but gains the town's respect. Cyrus walks the emptied infirmary and reads her own ledger aloud to the walls. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: reckoning — survival's price paid in full view.

chapters.title: The Regiment of Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Months later, a letter arrives from Nell, now apprenticed to a printer, the ledger set in type under its true title: the names of everyone the officers omitted. Cyrus joins the town's rebuilding, staying where she was needed all along. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging earned — history happened here, to her, and she stayed to carry it.
